answer.rationale: The recovered source records expose a systematic distortion in the consolidated memory layer: memory_73 records targeted promotional pricing as 'effective... with strong acquisition and revenue lift' while the archived source exp_73 shows signup +31% and qualified revenue +18% but 30-day retention -12%, with an explicit source-level instruction NOT to generalize discounting as sustainable growth. The consolidation step dropped the retention harm and the caveat. Since the primary objective is sustainable long-term qualified revenue, promotional_pricing is ruled out — it would buy a cohort that does not survive first renewal, and under a competitor price war it also invites a margin spiral we cannot win. Critically, the same summarization process that stripped the caveat from memory_73 produced memory_31, memory_57, memory_91, and memory_44; none of those have been checked against source, so their optimistic framings must be treated as possibly having lost similar retention-side caveats. I therefore act only on the one direction whose source record I have actually recovered and which was confirmed intact: exp_86 / memory_86, shortened onboarding (completion +13%, time-to-value -2.1 days, 30-day retention +3%) — the only candidate with verified positive retention, i.e. the only one directly aligned with sustainable revenue rather than acquisition volume. I choose standard_experiment rather than broad_rollout because exp_86 was measured on self-serve accounts and the present pressure is churn among existing price-sensitive SMB accounts; onboarding improvement does not directly address already-acquired at-risk accounts, so the transfer is unproven even though the underlying finding is sound. I am deliberately not treating this as a full answer to the competitor cut. Next cycle, when archive access returns, memory_73 should be corrected in place to carry the retention figure and the do-not-generalize conclusion, and memory_31/57/91/44 should be re-derived from source before any of them is used to justify a broad move — otherwise this distortion propagates into every future session that inherits this memory.
